caption_used: The character distribution in RoleplayPref is organized into three primary categories — Virtual Characters, Custom Characters, and Real Characters — with 13 subcategories in the outer ring. Virtual Characters occupy approximately 60% of the distribution and are subdivided into Comic Characters, Movie Characters, Teleplay Characters, Novel Characters, and Game Characters, with Movie Characters forming the largest virtual subcategory. Real Characters comprise seven subcategories including Scientists, Artists, Athletes, Writers, Musicians, Actors, and Influencers, with Musicians representing the largest real-character segment. Custom Characters occupy a small portion with no labeled subcategories.

The central sector, labeled “Custom Characters,” is a small, light green segment. Surrounding this central sector are three primary categories: “Virtual Characters,” “Real Characters,” and “Movie Characters,” each encompassing further subcategories. The “Virtual Characters” category, colored in light blue, is the largest segment, accounting for approximately 60% of the total distribution and is divided into five subcategories: “Comic Characters” (pink), “Movie Characters” (light blue), “Teleplay Characters” (dark blue), “Novel Characters” (purple), and “Game Characters” (orange). The “Real Characters” category, colored in light green, contains seven subcategories: “Scientists” (dark green), “Artists” (yellow), “Athletes” (red), “Writers” (brown), “Musicians” (light green), “Actors” (magenta), and “Influencers” (cyan). A legend is present, providing color-coded identification for each category and subcategory. No sectors are visually emphasized, and no percentages are displayed within the sectors.

raw_responses.English:
Let's analyze the figure step by step.

The chart is a circular pie chart designed to represent the distribution of character types within the RoleplayPref dataset. There are a total of thirteen distinct slices, arranged in a radial pattern around a central area. The largest slice, occupying approximately 60%, is labeled "Virtual Characters" and colored in a light blue shade. Within this slice, there are five subcategories: "Comic Characters" (pink), "Movie Characters" (light blue), "Teleplay Characters" (dark blue), "Novel Characters" (purple), and "Game Characters" (green). The next largest slice, representing approximately 20%, is labeled "Real Characters" and colored in a light green shade. This slice is further divided into seven subcategories: "Scientists" (dark green), "Artists" (yellow), "Athletes" (orange), "Writers" (red), "Musicians" (brown), "Actors" (light orange), and "Influencers" (magenta). The smallest slice, approximately 10%, is labeled "Custom Characters" and is not subdivided. Finally, a very small slice, representing approximately 10%, is labeled "Tealeplay Characters" and is colored in a dark blue shade. The chart does not include a legend or percentage labels within the slices, and no slices are visually emphasized. The slices appear to be ordered from largest to smallest in terms of their area.

The largest segment, representing Virtual Characters, occupies approximately 60% of the total area and is further divided into five subcategories: Comic Characters (red), Movie Characters (light blue), Teleplay Characters (dark blue), Novel Characters (purple), and Game Characters (green). The Real Characters segment, accounting for roughly 30% of the total, is subdivided into seven subcategories: Scientists (yellow), Artists (pink), Athletes (orange), Writers (brown), Musicians (light green), Actors (dark green), and Influencers (gray). The Custom Characters segment is a small portion of the chart with no labeled subcategories. Percentages are not explicitly indicated within the segments, but a legend is present to identify the colors associated with each category. The segments are arranged in a clockwise direction, starting with the largest segment and proceeding outwards.
